strategies.name: Naive Sequential All-Reduce Loop
strategies.desc: Eight sequential all_reduce calls with interleaved local bidiagonal coupling and uncoupling transformations, exactly as in the reference implementation. 8 all_reduce dispatches total. Represents the baseline: maximal correctness clarity, no fusion, highest dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Fused Bidiagonal Transform Batching
strategies.desc: Precompute all coupling coefficients and fuse the forward coupling and backward uncoupling operations into vectorized tensor operations before/after each all_reduce, reducing loop overhead. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but amortizes local computation cost through batched element-wise operations and potentially better cache locality.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all_reduce with a reduce_scatter followed by all_gather pair, performing the bidiagonal transformation on the smaller scattered shards between the two collectives. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on 1/W of the data, potentially better network utilization and allows overlapping local compute with smaller communication payloads.

strategies.name: Pipelined Two-Stage Macro-Batching
strategies.desc: Group the 8 stages into 4 pairs, where each pair fuses two consecutive coupling-reduce-uncoupling sequences by algebraically combining their transformations before issuing collectives. 4 all_reduce dispatches with more complex local preprocessing/postprocessing. Trades local compute complexity for halved collective dispatch count.

strategies.name: Ring-Based Custom Collective Pattern
strategies.desc:
Implement a custom ring all_reduce using point-to-point send/recv operations that integrates the bidiagonal coupling directly into the reduce-scatter and all-gather phases of the ring algorithm. Approximately 2*(W-1)*8 send/recv operations but eliminates the separation between reduction and coupling, potentially hiding coupling latency within communication phases.
